title: Homogeneous-normalized Rees cone comparison exists
statement: For any closed immersion $s:S\hookrightarrow V$, there exists an isomorphism $q$ from the extended-Rees zero fibre to the relative-Spec conormal cone satisfying $\operatorname{ReesConeNormalized}(s,q)$ [def-pur-rees-cone-normalization]. This asserts existence only; no uniqueness is asserted.

proof.text: On each ambient affine chart compose the conormal presentation chart with the proved homogeneous Rees/associated-graded isomorphism. Direct-sum and ideal-quotient induction on homogeneous representatives prove naturality for affine basic-open maps.

proof.text: Inverse images of ambient affine opens form a cover-dense and locally full basis on the closed subscheme. The basis sheaf-isomorphism theorem extends the chart isomorphisms. Constants show compatibility with the structure algebra. The affine-morphism/relative-Spec anti-equivalence then gives the scheme isomorphism and its pullback formula.

proof.text: Pulling a degree-one representative along the Rees zero section gives zero: transfer to the quotient-spec chart, apply normalConeToQuotient, and use extendedReesAlgebraToPolynomial_C_mul_T_neg_one. The relative-Spec zero section is induced by the conormal augmentation, so its degree-one pullback is zero as well. The proved degree-one morphism-detection theorem identifies the two sections.
